summary: Your past comes out: {rival} tells the press about {the old act}.
realLife: In his first House race in West Virginia in 1952, a primary opponent revealed his past Ku Klux Klan membership. Byrd said he had joined in the early 1940s and left; his Republican opponent later found a 1946 letter from Byrd to the Klan's leader. He won, and years later called joining the worst mistake of his life.
gates: {the old act} is on your record and a rival can find it.
choices: own it and say why you left
play it down (a lie if the record says more)
go on the air about it

branches.then: A letter in your own hand shows more than you said. A denial now is a caught lie.

branches.when: you call it the worst mistake of your life
branches.then: The line goes on your record and follows you.
